topic.name: Language Modeling
topic.description: Autoregressive sequence probability, contextual conditioning, and the limits of next-token objectives.

concepts.name: Autoregressive language modeling
concepts.description: Factoring a sequence probability into next-token conditionals over prior context while keeping learned parameters fixed at inference.

misconceptions.name: Parallel logits imply independent tokens
misconceptions.description: Mistakes parallel teacher-forced computation for a factorization that removes dependence on earlier tokens.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the sequence likelihood as a product of conditionals before reasoning about how those conditionals are computed.

misconceptions.name: Prompt conditioning retrains model weights
misconceptions.description: Treats an inference-time prompt as a parameter update rather than input context for a fixed model.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate changes to the conditional context from optimizer-driven changes to parameters.

misconceptions.name: Next-token likelihood certifies factuality
misconceptions.description: Equates probability under a text distribution with external truth or evidential support.
misconceptions.remediation: Distinguish modeling text continuation frequencies from verifying claims against the world.

questions.stem: A decoder is trained with teacher forcing, so logits for every position are computed in one parallel forward pass. Which statement correctly describes the modeled probability of the token sequence?

options.text: It remains a product of next-token probabilities conditioned on earlier tokens; parallel training does not remove that factorization.
options.rationale: Teacher forcing supplies every prefix at once, but each position still represents its conditional factor in the sequence likelihood.

options.text: It becomes a product of independent token marginals because positions whose logits are computed together no longer condition on prefixes.
options.rationale: Computational parallelism does not erase the causal context used by each position.

options.text: It is defined by prompt-specific weight updates because conditioning on earlier tokens retrains the decoder during each forward pass.
options.rationale: Conditioning changes activations and probabilities while the model parameters remain fixed during the forward pass.

options.text: It assigns factual confidence to the sequence because high teacher-forced likelihood verifies that each generated claim is externally supported.
options.rationale: Sequence likelihood describes fit to token patterns, not independent verification of factual claims.

questions.stem: Two prompts are sent to the same deployed language model with sampling disabled and no fine-tuning between requests. Why can the next-token distributions differ?

options.text: The model first predicts all tokens independently, then the prompt selects which marginal distribution should be exposed to the user.
options.rationale: Autoregressive predictions are conditional on context rather than selected from context-free token marginals.

options.text: The parameters stay fixed, while each prompt supplies a different prefix and therefore a different conditional next-token distribution.
options.rationale: Inference-time context changes hidden states and conditional probabilities without performing an optimizer update.

options.text: Each prompt performs a temporary training step on its own text, producing new weights that are discarded after the response.
options.rationale: Ordinary prompting is a forward-pass conditioning operation, not an implicit gradient update.

options.text: The prompt with the higher-probability continuation has supplied stronger evidence that the continuation's factual claims are correct.
options.rationale: Conditional probability under the model is not a factuality or source-support score.

questions.stem: An autoregressive model gives a fluent historical claim high continuation probability, but a trusted archive contradicts it. What conclusion follows from the language-model objective?

options.text: The contradiction occurs because the archive prompt silently retrained the model weights toward a different historical account.
options.rationale: Supplying or consulting context does not imply that the deployed model parameters were optimized again.

options.text: The claim should be accepted because a probable continuation under the text model carries stronger evidential status than an external record.
options.rationale: The objective learns token-distribution regularities and does not rank external sources by truth.

options.text: High continuation probability can reflect common textual patterns; factual acceptance still requires evidence outside the next-token likelihood.
options.rationale: Likelihood under a language model and warranted belief about the world are different quantities.

options.text: The archive and generated claim are independent token samples, so their disagreement does not reveal a limitation of conditional language modeling.
options.rationale: The generated claim is context-conditioned, and the disagreement directly exposes that text likelihood is not factual verification.

questions.stem: A deployed autoregressive model receives five worked examples in its prompt. Its parameter checksum is unchanged, yet its next-token predictions on a related query improve. Which explanation fits this observation?

options.text: The examples changed the conditional context processed by fixed parameters; they did not perform an optimizer update.
options.rationale: In-context examples alter the prefix and resulting activations while the deployed parameter values remain fixed.

options.text: The examples triggered a temporary gradient step, so the model used prompt-specific weights despite the unchanged checksum.
options.rationale: Ordinary prompting performs conditional inference, and an unchanged parameter checksum contradicts a weight update.

options.text: The model predicted context-free token marginals, then selected a better independent distribution after reading the examples.
options.rationale: Autoregressive logits are conditioned on the preceding context rather than chosen from independent token marginals.

options.text: The improved continuation score established that factual claims in the response gained external evidential support.
options.rationale: Improved conditional prediction does not independently verify claims against evidence about the world.

questions.stem: For a three-token sequence, a fixed autoregressive model assigns probabilities 0.50, 0.25, and 0.10 to each observed token conditioned on its preceding prefix. Which computation and interpretation are valid?

options.text: Multiply to obtain 0.0125, then interpret the factors as context-free marginals because their logits were computed in parallel.
options.rationale: The numerical product is right, but each factor is explicitly conditional on its prefix rather than a context-free marginal.

options.text: Multiply to obtain 0.0125, interpreting the result as the product of successive prefix-conditioned token probabilities.
options.rationale: The autoregressive chain rule assigns the sequence probability by multiplying the stated conditional factors.

options.text: Recompute the factors after a prompt-specific parameter update because conditioning each token retrains the model weights.
options.rationale: Prefix conditioning changes model inputs and activations without implying an optimizer step or new parameters.

options.text: Use the largest factor, 0.50, as the sequence's factual confidence because likelihood certifies external correctness.
options.rationale: Neither a token probability nor their product independently verifies the sequence's claims against external evidence.
